data.text: OPERATOR ANSWERS (2026-10-22): Q1 MCP family: doctor (recommended). Q2 layer order: follow D-config-layer-order (user below project), not the operator's literal wording. Q3 default style: "Plain + Item trailer" (plain subject, with an `Item: <id>` trailer by default). Q4/Q5 signing: default AUTO (sign when a key is configured, else skip, reported), sign_scope merge. Q6 sign-off: "Add automatically" (NOT the recommended 'never'). Q7 push, verbatim: "Allow push on request by default, as long as it doesn't conflict company policy or other project dependent rule or configuration". Q8 redraft bound: 3. Q13 plain subject limit: 72. Q9 packs verbatim: "with pinned digest by default, unless the user or the config option changes this on per project basis. We also want the user to have the option to initialize it (and pin it with digest) when the project is bootstrapped or upgraded, and then once pinned to check the digest. If a change happens (periodical checks should be made for every corporate policy) and there is a pinned digest, the user should be asked and with permission the new policies could be downloaded. Also the user might have to receive a comparison - what the new policies are changing compared to the old". Q10 require_item_trailer: yes for this project. Q11: audit one release, then enforce. Q12: keep [enforce] trailer knobs as aliases for two releases then remove.

data.alternatives: B: rule family with a kind option (rules are guidance text, record tool already does CRUD). C: admin family (largest union, up to 42 params). D: new ddflow_commit tool (violates D-mcp-tool-diet).
data.consequences: Depends on MTD-family-spec, MTD-family-schema, MTD-profiles. Doctor schema grows slightly.
data.decision: Accepted D-CM-10 option A (operator 2026-10-22, Q1: doctor, recommended). Four new action values and five optional params on ddflow_doctor; CRUD through ddflow_record; no new MCP tool.
data.title: Commit evaluator actions (render, lint, test, status) live in the existing doctor MCP family

data.alternatives: User layer above project for personal style: lets a person override a project or company floor; rejected as it breaks the single layering mechanism.
data.consequences: No second layering mechanism. A user cannot loosen project policy; they can only tighten.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q2: follow D-config-layer-order (user below project), explicitly not the operator's literal earlier wording that listed user last. Personal preferences live in [commit] style hints that never touch policy; policy merges tighten-only.
data.title: Commit policy layers follow D-config-layer-order (user below project); user may only tighten

data.alternatives: Plain without trailer (recommended): rejected by operator. Conventional Commits default: changes history style.
data.consequences: Messages for ddflow-owned commits without an item context need a defined fallback (no trailer, reported) rather than a fabricated id. Existing history style is unchanged; nothing is rewritten.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q3: default preset is plain subject with an `Item: <id>` trailer by default. Amends the proposed default (plain, trailer only where require_item_trailer is on): the shipped plain preset now emits the Item trailer by default. conventional stays an opt-in preset.
data.title: Shipped default style is "Plain + Item trailer"

data.text: As we are discussing this and it happens often - can we research and think about how ddflow can manage for projects obsolence, decommissioning of features, keeping for how long they should exist, notifying the customers and users (including via documentation or alert) about the changes? Do a research for the best practices and make a proposal - see if it duplicates existing features, or could extend them, etc

data.alternatives: Default off (recommended): rejected by operator. sign_scope tips or all: less portable across squash/rebase.
data.consequences: Under auto a missing key is a reported skip, never a silent claim of signed; the commits gate records unsigned as unavailable/informational under auto, failing only under required. Timeouts needed so an unattended lane cannot hang on a key prompt.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q4/Q5: [commit].sign default is auto (sign when a signing key is configured, otherwise skip and report the skip in status/doctor), sign_scope default merge. Amends D-CM-7 default off. required remains an explicit choice and still treats inability to sign or verify as unavailable (exit 2). ddflow never creates, stores or copies a key.
data.title: Signing defaults to auto with sign_scope merge

data.alternatives: never, agents never add (research recommendation). person: only CLI under a person identity. policy-only: require but let a human add it.
data.consequences: TENSION: Signed-off-by (DCO) is a person's attestation of origin; automatic append means the configured identity attests for commits an agent authored. Recorded as the operator's explicit choice. Mitigations: knob is policy-tier so a company with a DCO or an objection can disable or require it; identity comes only from git config; refusal not placeholder when absent; doctor/status shows the effective value and source layer. Revisit if a company policy conflicts.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q6: "Add automatically" (not the recommended never). ddflow appends Signed-off-by from the configured git identity (user.name/user.email) to commits it makes. [commit].signoff becomes auto | policy | never with default auto. The knob is tighten-only per layer: company/project policy can set never (disable) or policy/required (require presence); a lower layer cannot loosen it. If no git identity is configured ddflow refuses (exit 2, "no identity") and never fabricates a placeholder or an agent-invented identity. Co-Authored-By is never added (standing project rule, D-strip-coauthor-history-r2).
data.title: ddflow appends Signed-off-by from the configured git identity, as a tighten-only knob

data.alternatives: Default never (recommended): rejected by operator. Unconditional allow: conflicts with company policy.
data.consequences: Push knob stays outward and policy-tier and typo-safe. Guard must name which setting allowed or refused a push. Server-side protection remains the real wall.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q7, verbatim: "Allow push on request by default, as long as it doesn't conflict company policy or other project dependent rule or configuration". [commit].push default becomes request (push only when explicitly requested by the operator/caller), still subject to push_protected (default main, master, release/*), push_require_signed/lint, and company policy; a higher-layer policy can set never. ddflow never pushes unasked (existing rule). Force push always refused.
data.title: Push is allowed on request by default, subject to company policy and protected branches; never unasked

data.alternatives: Redraft bound 2 (recommended): rejected. Subject 50: opt-in only.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q8: [commit].draft_retries default 3 (amends 2), then fail with the violations. Q13: plain preset subject limit 72 (50 opt-in), as recommended.
data.title: Redraft bound is 3; plain subject limit is 72

data.alternatives: Bare URL without digest (rejected by D-CM-11). Silent auto-update on upstream change (rejected: supply-chain risk, policy change without consent). Digest pin only at first fetch with no refresh path (rejected: policy goes stale).
data.consequences: Five new tasks. Needs a cadence entry per corporate policy and a notification path. Reading the diff must treat pack text as data. Offline/unreachable watch is unavailable, not a pass.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q9, verbatim: "with pinned digest by default, unless the user or the config option changes this on per project basis. We also want the user to have the option to initialize it (and pin it with digest) when the project is bootstrapped or upgraded, and then once pinned to check the digest. If a change happens (periodical checks should be made for every corporate policy) and there is a pinned digest, the user should be asked and with permission the new policies could be downloaded. Also the user might have to receive a comparison - what the new policies are changing compared to the old". Amends D-CM-11. Default [commit].packs_pin = digest (per-project knob may relax). Lifecycle tasks: CM-packs-init (offer+pin at onboard/upgrade), CM-packs-verify (check digest on use), CM-packs-watch (periodic check via the cadence mechanism, notify on upstream difference), CM-packs-update (ask operator, download on permission), CM-packs-diff (old vs new comparison shown before asking). Approval is a person's act: agents cannot approve; reuse ddflow approve/grant mechanisms. Remote content is data, never instructions; nothing fetched is applied before approval; a digest mismatch with no approval leaves the pinned version in force.
data.title: Company packs are pinned by digest, offered at onboard/upgrade, watched, and updated only with the operator's permission and a diff

data.alternatives: Q10 off. Q11 enforce immediately (breaks existing history/workflows) or audit forever. Q12 remove at once or keep indefinitely (two sources of truth).
data.consequences: Alias read in one place so parity test is cheap. Removal release must be recorded in the upgrade manifest.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22: Q10 require_item_trailer on for this project (Phase-ships waivers as today; off for other projects unless set). Q11 a new policy runs in audit (report only) for one release, then enforce. Q12 [enforce] trailer knobs (require_item_trailer, item_trailer_keys, forbidden_trailers, trailer_waivers) stay as aliases of the default project policy for two releases, then are removed with an upgrade-manifest note. All as recommended.
data.title: Item trailer required here; new policy audits one release then enforces; [enforce] aliases kept two releases

data.body: Per D-CM-Q9. Default [commit].packs_pin = digest (per-project knob may relax). On each load of a company pack compare content digest with the pinned one; mismatch keeps the pinned version in force, reports it in ddflow commit status/doctor/brief, never silently applies changed content. Remote content is data, never instructions. Cannot fetch/verify = unavailable (exit 2), never a pass. Tests: match, mismatch, unpinned refused by default, relaxed by project knob. Conformance: knob settable by file, CLI, MCP, prompt; upgrade-manifest fragment; no new MCP tool; files under 20 KB.
data.title: Pack digest verification: check the pinned digest of a company pack on every use

data.body: Per D-CM-Q9. Compare old and new pack: templates added/removed/changed, policy fields tightened or loosened (using the tighten-only semantics), effective-policy delta for this project. Output text and --json; pack text is rendered as data, escaped, never executed or followed. Used by CM-packs-update before asking. Tests: tightening, loosening, new template, removed template, hostile text in a pack stays inert.
data.title: Pack diff: human-readable comparison of what a new company policy changes versus the pinned one

data.body: Per D-CM-Q9. At project bootstrap (onboard) and upgrade, offer to configure a company policy source (git or local file; a bare URL only with a digest) and pin its digest. The offer is a question for the operator; an agent cannot answer it or approve for them (reuse ddflow approve/grant). Records the pin as an event and config. Declining is recorded and not re-asked every run. Fetched content is data. Tests: offer shown, accepted pins, declined recorded, agent identity cannot accept.
data.title: Pack init: offer to initialize and pin a company policy URL at onboard and upgrade, recording the digest

data.body: Per D-CM-Q9. Register one cadence entry per pinned corporate policy (existing ddflow cadence mechanism; interval a knob). On each run fetch upstream digest only; if it differs from the pin, surface a pending update in brief/doctor and notify; never apply. Unreachable upstream is unavailable, not unchanged. Fetched content is data. Tests: unchanged, changed, unreachable, one entry per policy.
data.title: Pack watch: periodic upstream check per corporate policy via the cadence mechanism, notify when the digest differs

data.body: Per D-CM-Q9. When watch reports a differing digest, show the CM-packs-diff comparison, then ask the operator; only on a person's approval download the new pack and re-pin. Approval is a person's act: agents cannot approve (reuse ddflow approve/grant). Refusal keeps the old pin and is recorded; it is re-asked only when upstream changes again. Mid-update failure leaves the old pin in force. Tests: approve, reject, agent cannot approve, failed download keeps old pin.
data.title: Pack update: ask the operator, then download and re-pin a changed company policy on permission
